question: Why does Huygens construction consider only the forward envelope of secondary wavelets and not the backward envelope?

options.A: Both forward and backward envelopes must be taken because both represent equally observable new wavefronts.
options.B: Secondary wavelets spread in all directions, but the observed disturbance propagates forward from a given wavefront. The forward envelope gives the physically observed new wavefront; the backward envelope does not represent this progressive propagation from the source.
options.C: Only the backward envelope is used because light waves travel back towards the source after each wavefront.
options.D: The forward envelope is selected because it has larger amplitude, while the backward envelope has zero amplitude.
